documents.title: Dissecting the genetic architecture for maize prolificacy by combining QTL mapping and genome-wide association study.
documents.abstract: Maize prolificacy (ears per plant) is a vital domestication trait in maize that profoundly determines grain yield potential. Deciphering its genetic regulatory network is essential for improving yield performance and expanding germplasm diversity. Here, we performed multi-environment phenotypic evaluation on two RIL populations and one association panel. Integrative QTL mapping and GWAS uncovered 13 QTLs and 8 QTNs associated with maize prolificacy. The stable locus qP9-2 harbored two tissue differentiation-associated genes (Zm00001eb395530, Zm00001eb395480), while the significant SNPs within
documents.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement

documents.title: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reveals the 2'-O-methylation landscape and SNORD88B-guided FN1 modification in hepatocellular carcinoma.
documents.abstract: To systematically map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on messenger RNA (mRNA) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), characterize its distribution features and biological functions, and identify key C/D box small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) that regulate Nm modification along with their target genes, thereby providing a molecular basis for elucidating post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms in HCC.

documents.title: DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
documents.abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to

documents.title: MaxGeomHash bridges MinHash and FracMinHash for scalable similarity estimation using sub-linear k-mer sketching.
documents.abstract: With the surge in sequencing data generated from biological studies, designing scalable computational techniques has become essential. One effective strategy to enable large-scale computation is to extract k-mers from long sequences, and summarize large k-mer sets into random samples (a.k.a. sketches). These sketches enable rapid estimation of similarity metrics such as Jaccard or cosine, and thus facilitate scalable computations. Popular sketching tools in bioinformatics range from the MinHash algorithm to generate fixed-size sketches; to FracMinHash algorithm to retain a fraction of all k-me

documents.title: Genomic and biological characterization of exopolysaccharides produced by Streptococcus thermophilus CCASU-ST-S3 and CCASU-ST-S52, with statistical optimization and preliminary spectroscopic characterization of EPS-STS3.
documents.abstract: Streptococcus thermophilus is a key dairy starter capable of producing exopolysaccharides (EPS) with strain-dependent biosynthetic and biological properties. Two EPS-producing strains, STS3 and STS52, isolated from yogurt, were characterized genomically, and their partially purified EPS preparations underwent preliminary biological evaluation.

documents.title: ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality.
documents.abstract: As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies.

documents.title: Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.
documents.abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin organization shapes gene regulation by partitioning the genome into transcriptionally active and inactive compartments, with implications for prostate carcinogenesis. We integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical samples representing benign prostatic hyperplasia, primary prostate cancer (PC), and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Using a computational framework accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity, we characterized A/B chromatin compartment organization in aneuploid tumors. We identified recurrent shifts from inac

documents.title: hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.
documents.abstract: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no exis

documents.title: Beyond Mutations: A Seven-CpG DNA Methylation Signature for Predicting HRD in MMRd Colorectal Cancer.
documents.abstract: We previously identified a high level of molecular heterogeneity within mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) colorectal cancer (CRC). Despite MMRd CRC being typically considered suitable for immunotherapy, only less than half of the metastatic CRC (mCRC) patients achieve complete remission. Thus, the search for identifying new therapeutic targets has become extremely urgent. The use of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) has revolutionized the treatment of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) cancer; however, the HRD prevalence in CRC remains unclear. Here, we conducted an integra

documents.title: Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.
documents.abstract: Low-coverage whole-genome sequencing offers a scalable approach to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing in ovarian cancer. This multi-centre study describes the real-world implementation of one such assay, SeqOne SomaHRD, across four European laboratories between 9 January 2023 and 1 October 2025. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive if they had a Genomic Instability score (GIS) of ≥0.50 (GIS-high) and/or a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. GIS was generated from two bioinformatically derived measures of genomic instability: Large-scale Genomic Alterations (LGA) and Loss of Parental
documents.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD

documents.title: DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.
documents.abstract: Sequencing methods based on Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) have revolutionized the field of viral genomics. However, available analysis tools are often internet-dependent, have complex installation requirements, or lack graphical user interfaces (GUIs), limiting their use in laboratories with restricted internet access or limited bioinformatics expertise. Here we present DeGenRESOLVE, a pipeline designed for amplicon-based ONT resequencing where a reference genome is available. This pipeline does not perform de novo assembly but processes raw base-called ONT viral sequencing data offline i

documents.title: Epigenome-informed prioritization of bivalent chromatin SNPs enhances genomic prediction robustness: a proof-of-concept study in Pacific white shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei).
documents.abstract: Genomic selection has become a powerful tool for accelerating genetic improvement in animal breeding, yet its broader application is often limited by high genotyping costs and reduced predictive reliability across populations. Functional genomic annotations offer a promising strategy to prioritize biologically meaningful variants and improve prediction robustness. Here, using Pacific white shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei) as a model, we conducted a proof-of-concept study integrating whole-genome resequencing and phenotypic data from 972 individuals. High-resolution epigenomic maps were generated

documents.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
documents.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack

documents.title: Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.
documents.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) such as evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction in clinical genomics, yet their adversarial robustness remains underexplored. We present SafeGenes, an evaluation framework combining input-space attacks, a discrete single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt-triggered backdoor. Across cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets, iterative attacks severely degrade discrimination: projected gradient descent (PGD) reduces the area under the curve (AUC) by more than 30 percentage points, and

documents.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.
documents.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outli

documents.title: MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.
documents.abstract: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) supports precision medicine in cancer care, but accurate assessment of missense variant pathogenicity, especially for variants without established consensus, remains challenging. Various computational tools have been developed for variant functional prediction, but most current tools rely solely on variant-level features and do not capture the clinical context of individual patients. To address this limitation, we developed MARiO (Missense Alteration Risk identifier in Oncology), a machine-learning model that integrates variant-level features and patient-l

documents.title: Pooled multiplex amplicon massive parallel sequencing for high-throughput confirmation of whole-genome sequencing potentially pathogenic variants in patients with parkinsonism.
documents.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) identifies large numbers of genetic variants, although only a subset requires independent confirmation for clinical interpretation. Sanger sequencing remains the standard confirmation method but is impractical for large-scale variant verification. We developed and evaluated a strategy for variant confirmation based on multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing of pooled DNA samples. WGS data were obtained from 86 individuals, including patients with parkinsonism and controls. Variants were selected using phenotype-driven filtering, ClinVar classification, and pa

documents.title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis.
documents.abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces

documents.title: Genome-Guided Discovery of ShK-like Peptides from Sanderia malayensis with Anti-Amyloidogenic and Neuroprotective Activities.
documents.abstract: While jellyfish venom represents a promising bioresource for biotechnological applications, the extraction of adequate venom amounts and the isolation of pure toxins present significant technical bottlenecks. To overcome these difficulties, a pipeline utilizing bioinformatic analyses was established to identify toxin candidates from genomic datasets, subsequently validating their functions from chemical synthesis. Specifically, a high-quality, 144 Mb genome assembly of the jellyfish Sanderia malayensis was constructed using PacBio CLR long reads (38.2 Gb), Illumina short reads (24.5 Gb), and H

documents.title: Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time.
documents.abstract: Detection of long exact matches between a pair of genomes has historically been a fundamental operation in genomics. Similarly, detection of long exact matches between all pairs of haplotypes in a large panel of genotyping array data or whole-genome sequencing variant calls is a fundamental operation in population genetics. Thanks to various recent pangenome efforts, for the first time, large panels of high-quality genome assemblies are being constructed. Therefore, we propose the intersection of these two approaches: detection of long exact matches between all pairs of assemblies in panels of
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Disease-modifying therapies in development for post-traumatic epilepsy.
documents.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a chronic neurological disorder that develops following traumatic brain injury (TBI), a condition affecting nearly 69 million people worldwide. PTE accounts for 20% of acquired epilepsies and is characterized by spontaneous recurrent seizures and long-term neurological deficits. Current antiseizure medications primarily suppress early seizures but do not prevent epileptogenesis or improve long-term neurological dysfunction. This review critically evaluates the current landscape of disease-modifying therapies for PTE with an emphasis on pathophysiological basis,

documents.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P.
documents.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular d
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Multi-omics approaches to unravel the biological effects of DNA-binding small molecules.
documents.abstract: DNA-targeting ligands comprise a diverse class of molecules that bind either canonical duplex DNA or non-canonical DNA structures such as G-quadruplexes. The recent shift towards combining distinct omics approaches, including epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, is significantly expanding the understanding of the biological effects induced by these small molecules, capturing complex cellular perturbations across multiple molecular layers. Here, we report representative examples from recent literature that illustrate how multi-omics approaches have helped to uncover previ

documents.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans -regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.
documents.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans -QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap , a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans -QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans -eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Epigenetic profiling of neuroactive curcumin on histone signatures in breast cancer using gen3DNet.
documents.abstract: Aberrant epigenetic alterations are implicated in the transformation of normal cells into cancerous ones. Unlike genetic mutations, these dysregulations can be reversible and are potential targets for anticancer drugs. Curcumin, a natural plant-derived compound, has been shown to have anticancer effects and neuroprotective properties via its influence on epigenetic regulation. However, the precise nature of these epigenetic changes and the mechanisms driving them remain largely unexplored. Moreover, there is strong evidence linking the neuroactive properties of chemotherapy drugs in the treatm

documents.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
documents.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta

documents.title: A Batch-Processing Pipeline for RNA-seq Gene Abundance Estimation.
documents.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets provide valuable opportunities to investigate gene and transcript abundance across species, tissues, developmental stages, and experimental conditions. However, processing multiple datasets consistently remains challenging because sequencing runs may differ in library layout, read length, sequencing depth, metadata quality, and analytical settings. Existing RNA-seq workflows often depend on dedicated workflow managers, substantial computational infrastructure, or advanced bioinformatics expertise, which may limit their accessibility for routine analyses. We pr

documents.title: Co-mutation of KRAS and ARID1A correlates with the MSI/LINE-1 hypermethylation profile in endometrial carcinoma.
documents.abstract: The interaction between oncogenic signalling and epigenetics in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (EEC) is poorly defined. We investigated the potential association of KRAS-ARID1A co-mutation axis with a distinct hypermethylator phenotype, affecting focal MLH1 promoter methylation and global DNA methylation (LINE-1).

documents.title: CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.
documents.abstract: Molecular profiling has refined risk stratification in meningioma, but the biological relevance of associated transcriptional changes remains incompletely understood. Calbindin D28K (Calb), encoded by CALB1, is a calcium-binding protein with reported anti-apoptotic and cytoprotective functions. Previous unsupervised transcriptomic analysis identified CALB1 upregulation in meningiomas with aggressive cellular features, but its biological and clinical relevance remains unresolved. We analysed Calb immunoreactivity in 231 meningioma tissue microarray (TMA) cores from 147 patients and evaluated CA

documents.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.
documents.abstract: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses.
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
documents.abstract: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and

documents.title: Topological Data Analysis Identifies Copy Number Variation Subtypes of Bulls Associated with Fertility.
documents.abstract: Bull fertility is a polygenic trait of significant economic importance in dairy and beef cattle, controlled by multiple genetic variants, including copy number variations (CNVs). Conventional single-variant association analyses primarily evaluate marginal effects of individual loci, whereas CNV co-occurrence patterns require complementary approaches. This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to identify groups of bulls based on genome-wide CNVR profiles and to assess their association with insemination success rate. A total of 88 bulls were included, and the presence/absence of 406 co

documents.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
documents.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temp

documents.title: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel.
documents.abstract: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP . Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities.
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
documents.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions
documents.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

documents.title: Systematic benchmarking of Hi-C-based scaffolding methods in genome assembly.
documents.abstract: High-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) technology is crucial for scaffolding, a key step to generate chromosome-level high-quality genome assemblies. However, although several Hi-C-based scaffolding tools have been developed, their utility in genome assembly remains constrained by inconsistent performance, making a systematic benchmarking urgently needed. Here, we present a comprehensive benchmark of five prominent Hi-C scaffolders using simulated contig assemblies considering various factors, including contig lengths, chimeric contig proportions, Hi-C coverage depths, and ploi

documents.title: Correction of the cytosine deamination artifacts in FFPE-based sequencing experiments.
documents.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues remain an essential resource for molecular studies, yet formalin-induced cytosine deamination introduces characteristic C > T/G > A artifacts that compromise the accuracy of next-generation sequencing analyses. Numerous computational methods and enzymatic DNA repair strategies have been proposed to reduce these artifacts, but no systematic comparison across tools and experimental conditions exists. Here, we evaluate the performance of seven computational approaches (SOBDetector, Ideafix, MicroSEC, FFPolish, DeepOmics FFPE/FFPE-PLUS, FFPErase) to

documents.title: XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
documents.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i

documents.title: quarTeT after 3 years: toolkit updates and community insights for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly.
documents.abstract: Since its initial release in 2023, quarTeT has become a widely used toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and characterization. Here, we present a major update that improves all four quarTeT modules, including optional contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer (TE), and support for holocentric chromosomes in CentroMiner (CM). The main program has also been upgraded with user-configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and simplified deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity.

documents.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
documents.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.

documents.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
documents.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.

documents.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
documents.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera

documents.title: Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.
documents.abstract: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models.

documents.title: Gestational Pyrethroid Exposure and Placental Health in Wistar Rats: Evaluation of Epigenetic, Developmental, and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers.
documents.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms of placental toxicity provides an important research tool that can help to clarify how early-life exposure may influence adverse pregnancy outcomes, foetal health, and long-term disease risk in adulthood. In the present study we estimated the effects of oral gestational exposure to the pyrethroid insecticide α-cypermethrin (α-cyp), a potential endocrine disruptor, in doses of 1, 10, and 19 mg/kg bw/day on different parameters in placentas of Wistar rats (n = 5 per group; 30 animals in total). We evaluated global DNA methylation within the LINE1 repetitive region us

documents.title: In silico analysis toward functional genomic profiling and bioprospecting Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential.
documents.abstract: Proteases from bacteria and their secondary metabolites have bioactivity which can be utilized in therapeutical industries to overcome the negative effects of existing conventional medicines.

documents.title: Exploring the SWEET gene family and its role in root system architecture in Populus tomentosa.
documents.abstract: Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporters (SWEETs) facilitate sugar translocation and shape plant organ development, yet few studies have characterized their functions in root-related physiological processes in woody perennials.

documents.title: Genome-wide association study of growth-related traits in mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi): identification of cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes using single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models.
documents.abstract: Mandarin fish (S. chuatsi) is China's most economically important freshwater aquaculture species, yet selective breeding remains constrained by long generation intervals and limited genomic resources. We performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 Siniperca chuatsi individuals (minimum 10-fold coverage), retaining 1,310,398 quality-controlled bi-allelic SNPs across 24 chromosomes. Population structure analysis (principal component analysis, neighbor-joining, and ADMIXTURE) resolved four primary ancestral lineages that further separated into up to six finer-scale ancestry components, with evidenc

documents.title: Epigenetic modification of neurotransmitter pathways during fasting: a systematic review.
documents.abstract: Dietary restriction, encompassing intermittent fasting and caloric restriction, represents a prominent non-pharmacological approach to modulating brain aging and neuronal resilience. Emerging evidence links metabolism to long-term neural plasticity through epigenetic mechanisms, yet findings remain fragmented. This review integrates preclinical evidence on how dietary restriction alters brain epigenetic regulation and links these changes to neurocognitive outcomes.

documents.title: Discriminating malignancy of pulmonary nodules using a peripheral blood leukocyte DNA methylation-based SEMO network model.
documents.abstract: Accurately discriminating malignant pulmonary nodules from benign lesions remains challenging, particularly in subcentimeter lesions. This study developed and internally validated a peripheral blood leukocyte (PBL) DNA methylation-derived Selective Epigenomic Module Optimization (SEMO) network model to improve risk stratification.
